rules: Import `ruststream_rdkafka::prelude::*` at a mount site; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds an injected slot with a capability, the one exception being a body that writes a per-record setting.

Pick the descriptor by what a subscription reads: `KafkaTopic` for one topic, `KafkaTopics` for several or a `^` pattern, `KafkaPartitions` for a fixed partition list without a group, or bare `#[subscriber("orders")]` in the broker's `default_group`.
Keep per-key order under concurrency with `workers(n, by_key)`; the descriptor's `lane_key` picks the lane key: `LaneKey::Partition` (the default, keyless records included) or `LaneKey::RecordKey`.

Rebuild from the log with `start_at(KafkaPosition::earliest())` (or a timestamp) on every startup; move a running subscription from its handler with `Ctx<SeekHandle>`, a local seek that commits nothing and a rebalance discards.

Name `Commit::Tracked` on the descriptor whenever a handler settles deliveries itself; under the default `Commit::Auto` librdkafka stores the position on delivery, so `ack` and `nack(false)` are advisory and a requeue reports `AckError::Unsupported`.

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(topic)` after `include` (Kafka counts none); a `KafkaTopics` or `KafkaPartitions` mount names the copy's topic: `.out_retry(policy).to(topic)` or `.out_retry(policy).transform(ToSourceTopic)`.

Set a record's partition with the per-message setting `partition(n)` on the publish builder, bounding the slot `Out<impl Publisher<Options = KafkaOptions>, Marker>`; the framework's partition-key header becomes Kafka's native record key.

Give each concurrent transactional flow its own `transactional_id` (a second producer on one id fences the first): `per_partition()` with `Out<impl PartitionLanes>` for a worker pool; `EosPublish`, `Commit::Transactional(id)` and `EosReplies` for EOS.

Prefer a registry-backed codec (`AvroCodec`, or `SchemaFramed` over `JsonCodec`) with `KafkaBroker::schema_prefetch`; `KafkaBroker::schema_registry` plus `SchemaFrame` is the JSON transcode compatibility path, and the two never sit on one broker.

Carry a Protobuf message on the core's byte lanes with `#[wire(..)]` and frame it at publish time with `KafkaPublish::framed(&registry)` or the app-wide `ProtobufFrame` layer; a `prost` message can never be a codec's value.

Test a service by handing the app `main` runs to `ruststream::testing::TestApp::start`, which connects `KafkaBroker` in process with the `testing` feature, and address it as `tb.broker::<KafkaBroker>()`; write no mocks and build no second app.
Run the in-process test body against a running cluster with `TestApp::start_live` for what only Kafka has; keep `TestApp::start` for the rest of the suite.

Reach any librdkafka property this crate does not surface through `KafkaBroker::config`, `KafkaBroker::producer_config` or the descriptor's `config`, which is applied last and wins over the typed options.
